missing: A direct pick that meets all three constraints at once, with battery life measured on an iPhone with notifications on (not the maker's rated days), plus current prices and which iOS features (notification replies, calls, Apple Health sync) actually work.
why: The only major reviewer present is TechRadar, and its three pages answer neighbouring questions: best for iPhone overall, best smartwatch overall, best fitness tracker, with budget picks rated 5–10 days or 18 hours, never the two-week/$200/iPhone combination. Tom's Guide is off-target and both Wareable slots are empty. What actually addresses the question is one niche site claiming unverifiable tests and four spec-only or recycled-domain listicles (one impersonating Tom's Guide). A focused page naming the iPhone-compatible watches that genuinely reach two weeks under $200, with current prices, would stand out.
